summary.one_liner: Telephone is a VoIP SIP softphone for macOS that lets you make phone calls over the internet or a company network.
summary.what_it_does: Telephone is a SIP softphone for Mac, so a phone line that supports the SIP protocol can be used on a Mac in place of a physical phone wherever there is a reasonable network connection. The README describes it only as a softphone for making calls over the Internet or a company network. It has an optional Opus codec. The README covers only the build process: it asks you to build third-party dependencies (Opus, LibreSSL, and PJSIP, a SIP library) with configure/make scripts and patches, then build Telephone itself. It does not document end-user setup, account configuration, or a feature list beyond this.
use_cases: make VoIP calls from a Mac
use a SIP phone line on a computer
replace a desk phone with a Mac app
place calls over a company network
how_to_run: Download and build Opus (optional codec) with ./configure, make, make install into ThirdParty/Opus
Download, verify, and build LibreSSL into ThirdParty/LibreSSL
Download pjproject-2.10, create pjlib/include/pj/config_site.h with the listed defines
Apply the three patches in ThirdParty/PJSIP/patches with patch -p0
Configure, make lib, and make install PJSIP with the --with-opus and --with-ssl prefixes
stack: Objective-C/Swift (macOS app, inferred from macOS focus; not named in README)
notable: Turns a Mac into a SIP softphone as an alternative to a physical phone
Builds universal binaries for arm64 and x86_64
Dependencies are built from source with bundled patches
Pull requests are not accepted; feedback goes through issues
caveats: Requires building PJSIP, LibreSSL, and optionally Opus from source before the app can be built
Pull requests are not accepted for legal reasons; only issues for feedback
